notes.text: Given me — This and the following passages may be in some sort understood of the prophet Isaiah, but they are far more evidently and eminently verified in Christ, and indeed seem to be meant directly of him. The tongue - All ability of speaking plainly, and convincingly, and persuasively. Weary - Burdened with the sense of his, deplorable condition. Wakeneth - Me, from time to time, and continually. To hear - He by his Divine power assists me to the practice of all his commands and my duties, with all attention and diligence.
I gave — I patiently yielded up myself to those who smote me.

Justifieth — God will clear up my righteousness, and shew by many and mighty signs and wonders, that I lived and died his faithful servant. Let him come - l am conscious of mine own innocency, and I know that God will give sentence for me.
They — Mine accusers and enemies. The moth - Shall be cut off and consumed by a secret curse.

glossa.text: *The Lord hath given,* etc. ((ID.)) Although these things can be referred to Isaias, yet properly they are referred to Christ, as though he said: I who once wrought such things can now also work the like; my power is not diminished.

*As a garment.* ((ID.)) A garment is consumed by age and by the moth. The Jews too were called to penance for forty-two years after the Passion: at last, being negligent, they were crushed when the Romans came, and devoured by the moth of an evil conscience.

notes.text: Grief — With continual weeping.
Iniquity — For the punishment of mine iniquity. Consumed - The juice and marrow of them bring almost dried up with grief.
A fear — They were afraid to give me any countenance or assistance. Fled - To prevent their own danger and ruin.
A broken vessel — Which is irreparable, and useless, and therefore despised by all.
Fear — Just cause of fear.
My times — All the affairs and events of my life, are wholly in thy power.

glossa.text: *In a spacious place.* ((CASS.)) The spacious place of going freely to the fatherland of the virtues is charity: but because the flesh is weak and evils press: *Have mercy on me, O Lord.* Now the dread is recounted, that is, how many and how great are the things that disturb, against which is the prayer, *I am troubled.* ((AUG.)) Since he said before: *Thou hast set my feet in a spacious place,* etc. But for some the place is spacious, out of the thanksgiving of deliverance; for others, out of tribulation, it is a narrow strait. *Troubled.* He is angry for the sins of the chaff, etc., *as far as* for the life of the perfect is the advancement of others. *In anger the eye.* In the anger of the persecutors, etc., *as far as* that God may be sought from every degree. ((CASS.)) Or the understanding is disturbed and the mind confounded, etc., *as far as* neither in mind nor in body can there be any presumption of man. ((AUG.)) Anger through vice blinds the eye of the mind; anger through zeal troubles it: because this too, the mind being shaken, scatters contemplation, which is not except with an unquiet mind; but thereafter, after a little, it profits the more toward seeing.
*In poverty.* ((ID.)) Or *in want.* I lack health of body, and the torments are not spared. I lack release, and death is spared; and in this my confidence has been weakened.

*Above all my enemies.* ((ID.)) They live worse than the pagans and the Jews, etc., *as far as* for whom even their acquaintance are afraid, lest all be such. ((CASS.)) Or, among all my enemies, or, held in greater reproach than those who are worthy of it; and *to my neighbours,* to kinsfolk, or to those about to believe; and *to my acquaintance,* to those of the household.

*They that saw me without.* ((HIER.)) *Without,* Christ, that is, those who thought him a mere man. *I am forgotten as one dead from the heart.* ((CASS.)) Or, I have fallen out of their heart, like a dead man whose memory is buried with his body, of whose restoration there is despair. *A vessel that is destroyed,* Jesus dead is thought fit to be cast away.

*The blame of many.* ((AUG.)) They are blamed, etc., *as far as* not any man. *Round about. In that while they assembled together.* ((CASS.)) Of errors, etc., *as far as* that is, by the appetite of temporal things.

*My lots.* ((ID.)) Or, the times of life. ((AUG.)) Because we live or die when thou wilt: therefore *deliver.* Although the order of election is with thee, just and hidden, yet I, etc., *as far as* which, without merits, chooses whom it will.

*Illumine.* ((CASS.)) Make thy good will manifest upon me, that as they despair of the dying, so they may have confidence in the rising. ((AUG.)) *Illumine.* Let it appear who belongs to thee, since now there is confusion; whence elsewhere: *Distinguish my cause ((Psal. XLI))*; yet lest he seem to justify himself, he adds: *Save me in mercy,* not in my own justice.

notes.text: Who being in the essential form — The incommunicable nature. Of God - From eternity, as he was afterward in the form of man; real God, as real man. Counted it no act of robbery - That is the precise meaning of the words, - no invasion of another's prerogative, but his own strict and unquestionable right. To be equal with God - the word here translated equal, occurs in the adjective form five or six times in the New Testament, Matt. xx, 12; Luke vi, 34; John v, 18; Acts xi, 17; Rev. xxi, 16. In all which places it expresses not a bare resemblance, but a real and proper equalitg. It here implies both the fulness and the supreme height of the Godhead; to which are opposed, he emptied and he humbled himself.

Yet — He was so far from tenaciously insisting upon, that he willingly relinquished, his claim. He was content to forego the glories of the Creator, and to appear in the form of a creature; nay, to be made in the likeness of the fallen creatures; and not only to share the disgrace, but to suffer the punishment, due to the meanest and vilest among them all. He emptied himself - Of that divine fulness, which he received again at his exaltation. Though he remained full, John i, 14, yet he appeared as if he had been empty; for he veiled his fulness from the sight of men and angels. Yea, he not only veiled, but, in some sense, renounced, the glory which he had before the world began. Taking - And by that very act emptying himself. The form of a servant - The form, the likeness, the fashion, though not exactly the same, are yet nearly related to each other. The form expresses something absolute; the likeness refers to other things of the same kind; the fashion respects what appears to sight and sense. Being made in the likeness of men - A real man, like other men. Hereby he took the form of a servant.

And being found in fashion as a man — A common man, without any peculiar excellence or comeliness. He humbled himself - To a still greater depth. Becoming obedient - To God, though equal with him. Even unto death - The greatest instance both of humiliation and obedience. Yea, the death of the cross - Inflicted on few but servants or slaves.

Wherefore — Because of his voluntary humiliation and obedience. He humbled himself; but God hath exalted him - So recompensing his humiliation. And hath given him - So recompensing his emptying himself. A name which is above every name - Dignity and majesty superior to every creature.

That every knee — That divine honour might be paid in every possible manner by every creature. Might bow - Either with love or trembling. Of those in heaven, earth, under the earth - That is, through the whole universe.
And every tongue — Even of his enemies. Confess that Jesus Christ is Lord - Jehovah; not now "in the form of a servant," but enthroned in the glory of God the Father.

glossa.text: *For let this be your mind,* etc. As if to say: Let each one not seek his own advantage, but that of others, as Christ did. To patience and to humility I invite you. For you ought to be minded in yourselves in that which was in Christ. As Christ sought not his own things, but ours, so let us bear one another's burdens.

*Who being in the form.* He sets high things concerning Christ before all else, that those in whom there is place for abasement may not disdain to be humbled. *He thought it not robbery.* By usurping what would not be his own, as did the devil and the first man. Or, he did not judge himself to be equal to God according to his humanity, which would have been to commit robbery, that is, to presume upon what is not his own. *But he emptied himself.* The height having been shown, he adds concerning the humility.

((Aug., Ench. c. 35 et 36)). But he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, etc., *as far as* it came about that the man Christ could have no sin.

*The form of a servant.* Not losing the form of God: the form of a servant came to him, the form of God did not depart: *He emptied himself.* To empty oneself is to show oneself visible out of the greatness of his own invisibility.
*Made.* According to the form of a servant, he who was unmade according to the form of God, and also by his own *Habit.* That is, by his manner of life.
*He humbled himself,* etc. ((CHRYS.)) Of his own accord the Son obeyed the Father, not as though into a servile, etc., *as far as* that he honoured the Father most of all.
*For which cause.* The humility of Christ having been shown, which appeared chiefly in the passion; now he shows concerning his [Christ's] glory, and what and how much humility merits.

*That in the name.* Here he opens to whom the name of God has been given, to whom every creature bends the knee, that is, to God. But perhaps it might be said that the man was God by adoption, and thus Christ in part true God, in that in part he will be adoptive. But the creature does not bend the knee to an adoptive God, but to a true one. Yet it is agreed that Christ is true God, to whom the knee is bent, not adoptive.

*That the Lord,* etc. Which here certain men deny, saying: How can it come to pass that a man should be in the glory of God the Father? but if he be adoptive, a man who is God cannot be in the glory of God the Father.

notes.text: Matt. xxvi, 1; Luke xxii, 1.
Matt. xxvi, 6.
Some had indignation — Being incited thereto by Judas: and said - Probably to the women.
Judas went to the chief priests — Immediately after this reproof, having anger now added to his covetousness. Matt. xxvi, 14; Luke xxii, 3.
Matt. xxvi, 17; Luke xxii, 7.
Go into the city, and there shall meet you a man — It was highly seasonable for our Lord to give them this additional proof both of his knowing all things, and of his influence over the minds of men.
Furnished — The word properly means, spread with carpets.
Matt. xxvi, 20; Luke xxii, 14.

This is my blood of the New Testament — That is, this I appoint to be a perpetual sign and memorial of my blood, as shed for establishing the new covenant, that all who shall believe in me may receive all its gracious promises.
I will drink no more of the fruit of the vine, till I drink it new in the kingdom of God — That is, I shall drink no more before I die: the next wine I drink will not be earthly, but heavenly.
Matt. xxvi, 30; Luke xxii, 39; John xviii, 1.

This night — The Jews in reckoning their days began with the evening, according to the Mosaic computation, which called the evening and the morning the first day, Gen. i, 5. And so that which after sunset is here called this night is, ver. 30, called today. The expression there is peculiarly significant. Verily I say to thee, that thou thyself, confident as thou art, today, even within four and twenty hours; yea, this night, or ever the sun be risen, nay, before the cock crow twice, before three in the morning, wilt deny me thrice. Our Lord doubtless spoke so determinately, as knowing a cock would crow once before the usual time of cock crowing. By chap. xiii, 35, it appears, that the third watch of the night, ending at three in the morning, was commonly styled the cock crowing. Zech. xiii, 7.
Matt. xxvi, 36.

Sore amazed — The original word imports the most shocking amazement, mingled with grief: and that word in the next verse which we render sorrowful intimates, that he was surrounded with sorrow on every side, breaking in upon him with such violence, as was ready to separate his soul from his body.
Abba, Father — St. Mark seems to add the word Father, by way of explication.
Saith to Peter — The zealous, the confident Peter.
Matt. xxvi, 47; Luke xxii, 47; John xviii, 2.
Whomsoever I shall kiss — Probably our Lord, in great condescension, had used (according to the Jewish custom) to permit his disciples to do this, after they had been some time absent.
Matt. xxvi, 51; Luke xxii, 49; John xviii, 10.

A young man — It does not appear, that he was one of Christ's disciples. Probably hearing an unusual noise, he started up out of his bed, not far from the garden, and ran out with only the sheet about him, to see what was the matter. And the young men laid hold on him - Who was only suspected to be Christ's disciple: but could not touch them who really were so.
Matt. xxvi, 57; Luke xxii, 54; John xviii, 12.

All the council sought for witness and found none — What an amazing proof of the overruling providence of God, considering both their authority, and the rewards they could offer, that no two consistent witnesses could be procured, to charge him with any gross crime. Matt. xxvi, 59.
Their evidences were not sufficient — The Greek words literally rendered are, Were not equal: not equal to the charge of a capital crime: it is the same word in the 59th verse.

We heard him say — It is observable, that the words which they thus misrepresented, were spoken by Christ at least three years before, John ii, 19. Their going back so far to find matter for the charge, was a glorious, though silent attestation of the unexceptionable manner wherein he had behaved, through the whole course of his public ministry.
Matt. xxvi, 63; Luke xxii, 67.
Matt. xxvi, 69; Luke xxii, 56; John xviii, 25.
And he covered his head — Which was a usual custom with mourners, and was fitly expressive both of grief and shame.
Matt. xxvii, 1, 2; Luke xxii, 66; Luke xxiii, 1; John xviii, 28.
Matt. xxvii, 12.
Insurrection — A crime which the Roman governors, and Pilate in particular, were more especially concerned and careful to punish.

Will ye that I release to you the king of the Jews — Which does this wretched man discover most? Want of justice, or courage, or common sense? The poor coward sacrifices justice to popular clamour, and enrages those whom he seeks to appease, by so unseasonably repeating that title, The king of the Jews, which he could not but know was so highly offensive to them.
Praetorium — The inner hall, where the praetor, a Roman magistrate, used to give judgment. But St. John calls the whole palace by this name. Matt. xxvii, 27; John xix, 2.
Purple — As royal robes were usually purple and scarlet, St. Mark and John term this a purple robe, St. Matthew a scarlet one. The Tyrian purple is said not to have been very different from scarlet.
Matt. xxvii, 31; John xix, 16.
The father of Alexander and Rufus — These were afterward two eminent Christians, and must have been well known when St. Mark wrote.
Matt. xxvii, 33; Luke xxiii, 33; John xix, 17.
St. Mark seems to intimate, that they first nailed him to the cross, then parted his garments, and afterward reared up the cross.
Isaiah liii, 12.
Matt. xxvii, 39.
Matt. xxvii, 45; Luke xxiii, 44.
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me — Thereby claiming God as his God; and yet lamenting his Father's withdrawing the tokens of his love, and treating him as an enemy, while he bare our sins.
Matt. xxvii, 50; Luke xxiii, 46; John xix, 30.
Who served him — Provided him with necessaries.
Because it was the day before the Sabbath — And the bodies might not hang on the Sabbath day: therefore they were in haste to have them taken down.

honourable — A man of character and reputation: A counsellor - A member of the sanhedrim. Who waited for the kingdom of God - Who expected to see it set up on earth. Matt. xxvii, 57; Luke xxiii, 50; John xix, 38.
He rolled a stone — By his servants. It was too large for him to roll himself.

glossa.text:
*Now it was the pasch. ((HIER.))* Pascha is interpreted a passing over, but phase an immolation, etc., *as far as* and armed with virtue let us eat, saying: *For Christ our pasch is sacrificed ((Matth. XXVI))*.

((BEDA.)) Pascha, which in Hebrew is phase, from a passing over, not from suffering, etc., *as far as* it admonishes us, namely, to undertake the way of the virtues. *And the chief priests sought. ((HIER.))* Iniquity went forth from the princes, who ought to have made ready the temple, and the vessels, and to have purified themselves according to the law for the eating of the lamb.
*Not on the festival day. ((ID.))* They shun the festival day, and that befits them: there is no festival for those who have lost life and mercy.

*And when he was in Bethany. ((ID.))* The young hart of the harts always returns to his own bed, that is, the Son obedient to the Father even unto death: he asks obedience of us. For Simon is interpreted obedient. *Of Simon the leper.* Simon the leper signifies the world unbelieving at first, afterwards believing. *And as he was at meat, there came,* etc. He himself reclining, that is, humbling himself, that the faith of the sinful woman might touch him: which faith goes up from the feet to the head, and comes down from the head through faith, that is, from Christ to his members.

*A woman. ((BEDA.))* Mary Magdalen, the sister of Lazarus whom the Lord raised up, etc., *as far as* she poured holy oil upon him, as Matthew and Mark relate.

*An alabaster box.* Alabaster is a white marble marked with divers drops, and it keeps ointments uncorrupted. *Of spikenard.* Nard is called pistic, that is, mixed, because it was compounded not of the root only, but of the spikes and of the leaves: which is the more precious.

*And breaking. ((HIER.))* The house filled with the odour is heaven and earth. The broken alabaster is carnal desire, which is broken at the head: from which the whole body is framed together. ((BED.)) The devotion of Mary designates the faith and the piety of the Church, etc., *as far as* she venerates him with pious preaching and with devout observances.

*And there were some. ((ID.))* By synecdoche he put the plural for the singular, etc., *as far as* whose habit of thieving he took care for this cause to make known. *To what purpose is this waste. ((HIER.))* He that was lost found perdition out of salvation, so that in a fruitful fig tree he might light upon the noose of death.
*For this ointment might have been. ((ID.))* Under the pretext of avarice he speaks the mystery of faith, etc., *as far as* let us divide the spoils at evening.

*She hath wrought a good work. ((ID.))* He who believes in God, it is reputed to him unto a work of justice. For it is one thing to believe him, another to believe in him, that is, to cast oneself wholly upon him.

*But me you have not always. ((BEDA.))* Joined to you by bodily presence and familiarity as now. Whence the Apostle: *Although we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him ((II Cor. V))* . But spiritually he is always with us, whence: *Behold I am with you even to the consummation of the world all days. ((HIER.))* Thus is it to be understood: But me you shall not always have in bodily presence, as before in companionship and familiarity.
*What she had.* What you think to be a waste of the ointment is the office of burial. Nor is it a wonder if she has given me the good odour of faith, since I am about to shed my blood for her.

*Amen I say to you. ((BEDA.))* Note in Christ the knowledge of things to come, those about to suffer after a few days, he foreknows that his Gospel is to be preached in the whole world. It is to be noted that, as Mary through the whole world in which the Church is spread abroad earned glory for the loving service which she devoutly rendered to the Lord: so also Judas, who disparaged her, is defamed far and wide with the mark of perfidy. But the Lord rewards the good with loving praise, and is silent about the coming reproaches of the wicked man.

*One of the twelve. ((HIER.))* One in number, not in merit, in name not in divine power, in body not in mind, whence the bridegroom to the bride: *Thou hast wounded my heart, my sister, with one of thy eyes, and with one hair of thy neck ((Cant. IV))*. The eye and the hair are wisdom and virtue, since it is said to Judas with the rest: *To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God ((Matth. XIII))*. And: *I have given you power ((Luc. X))*, etc.

*He went to,* etc. He went away to the princes: and after he went out, Satan entered into him. Here *night to night showeth knowledge. Every living thing is joined to that which is like itself ((Matth. XXVIII))*. Mary runs to the apostles, that day to day may utter speech; Judas to the Jews, that night to night may show knowledge.

*And he sought how he might,* etc. ((HIER.)) He promises to betray him, as his master had said before: To thee will I give all this power. *BEDA.* Many today shudder at the crime of Judas and yet do not beware of it, etc., *as far as* that, the witnesses being removed, they may exchange truth for a lie, and virtue for a crime.

*And on the first day of the unleavened bread. ((Id.))* On the fourteenth moon, when, the leaven being cast away, the lamb was slain at evening, etc., *as far as* he consecrated the beginning of that very immolation, that is, of his own passion.

((ISID.)) With bitterness is the unleavened bread eaten, which is our redemption. For the bitterness is the passion of the Lord.

*Go into the city. ((BED.))* It is a token of the foreknowledge of his godhead, etc., *as far as* and that the baptism of the life-giving font may be consecrated for the taking away of the crimes of the world. ((HIER.)) The city is the Church, which is girt with the wall of faith: the man who meets them is the primitive people, the pitcher of water the law of the letter. *A man carrying a pitcher of water. ((BEDA.))* Of set purpose are the names both of the water-bearer and of the master of the house passed over in silence, that it may be signified that the opportunity is to be given to all who wish to keep the true pasch, that is, to be steeped in the sacraments of Christ, and who seek to receive him into the lodging of their own mind.

*Follow ye. ((HIER.))* He who leads on high, where the refreshment of Christ is, whence Rahab charges the spies to go not by the low places but by the heights.

*A large upper room. ((ID.))* The great Church, which declares the name of the Lord, strewn with the variety of the virtues and of tongues, whence: *Surrounded with variety ((Psal. XLIV))* of virtues, in which the pasch is prepared for the Lord. The master of the house is Peter the apostle, to whom the Lord entrusted his house: that there may be one faith under one shepherd. ((BED.)) The upper room is the spiritual law, which, going out from the straits of the letter, receives the Saviour in a lofty place, etc., *as far as* because it knows that all the sacraments of the pasch and the other decrees of the law are his sacraments.

*And in the evening. ((HIER.))* The evening of the day points to the evening of the world. For about the eleventh hour come the last: who first receive the penny of eternal life: because before the cross Abraham was in hell, and after the cross the thief was in paradise.

*Amen I say,* etc. As he had foretold of his passion: so he foretells of the betrayer, giving place for repentance, that when he had understood that his thoughts were foreknown by God, he might repent of his deed. Yet he does not point him out by name, lest, being openly refuted, he become more shameless. He casts the crime into the number: that he who is conscious of it may do penance. *One of you.* While falsehood is reproved, truth is proved and fulfilled. *He that did eat my bread, hath greatly supplanted me ((Psal. XL))*. All are touched, that harmony may be made in the harp. All the strings, being well strung, answer with a concordant voice: *Is it I, Lord?* One, slack and moved by the love of money, said: *Is it I, Rabbi?*

*To be made sorrowful.* As the eleven, because they had thought nothing evil against the Lord: but they believe their master more than themselves, and fearing their own frailty, sorrowful they ask concerning their own sin, of which they had no consciousness.

*One of the twelve. ((HIER.))* The wolf separates apart the sheep which he desires. The sheep which goes out of the fold lies open to the bites of the wolf. *He that dippeth. ((BEDA.))* Wonderful is the patience of the Lord. First he said: *One of you shall betray me,* the betrayer persists in his evil. He reproves more openly: and yet he is not named outright. Judas, when the others are made sorrowful and draw back their hand from the food, with the rashness and shamelessness with which he betrays the Lord; puts his hand also with his master into the dish, that by boldness he might feign a good conscience.
*But woe. ((ID.))* For ever woe to that man who comes unworthily to the table of the Lord, etc., *as far as* the punishment is foretold, that he who is not overcome by shame may be corrected by fear.

*As they were eating. ((ID.))* The old pasch being ended, which was kept in commemoration of the deliverance of the people of God from Egypt, etc., *as far as* and therefore that he was to be raised the more swiftly from death. *He took. ((HIER.))* Figuring his own body in the bread, etc., *as far as* the enemies are extinguished, which are the mysteries of the Church of Christ. ((BEDA.)) The bread which strengthens the heart of man, etc., *as far as* or that we are saved without his passion.

*Thanks.* He gave thanks and blessed, being now near to his passion, he who takes upon himself the punishment of another's iniquity: who did nothing worthy of suffering: that he might show with how even a mind every man ought to bear the scourges of his own fault.

*They had drunk. ((HIER.))* Happy drunkenness: saving fulness, etc., *as far as* for the blood of the New Testament which is shed for many cleanses not all.

*Now I will not drink. ((ID.))* Here he changes the sacrifice, but he does not change the time; so that we should never keep the supper of Jesus before the fourteenth moon. He who makes the resurrection on the fourteenth, keeps the supper of the Lord on the eleventh, which has never been found either in the New or in the Old Testament. *The vine. ((BEDA.))* The vine or the vineyard of the Lord is the Synagogue, etc., *as far as* I shall be filled with a new joy together with you over the salvation of that same people regenerated by baptism.

VERS. 26. *And a hymn being said. ((ID.))* It can be understood as the hymn which, according to John, he sang, giving thanks to the Father, etc., *as far as* and that we ought to ascend by the graces of the Holy Spirit with which we are anointed in the heart. *Unto the mount of Olives. ((HIER.))* On Mount Olivet Jesus is held fast: and thence he ascends to the heavens: that we may know that we ascend to the heavens from that place where we watch, and pray, and are bound, and do not fight back on the earth.

*You shall all be scandalized. ((BEDA.))* He foretells what they shall suffer: that when they have suffered they may not despair, but repent.

*In this night. They who are drunk, are drunk in the night ((I Thess. V))*, and they who are scandalized, are scandalized in the night, that is, being darkened in mind. ((HIER.)) All fall, but not all lie prostrate. *Because he sleepeth, shall he not rise again? ((Zach. XIII.))* To fall is carnal: to lie prostrate is devilish. *I will strike the shepherd.* Strike the shepherd. The prophet asks for the passion of the Lord: the Father answers: *I will strike the shepherd.* At the prayers of the saints the Son is sent by the Father: that is, he is made flesh and is struck, and suffers: the sheep are scattered, the shepherd being taken. The resurrection is promised, that hope be not extinguished.
*But Peter. ((ID.))* A bird without feathers strives to fly on high: but the body weighs down the soul, so that, by the fear of a human death, the fear of the Lord is overcome.

*The cock shall twice give voice. ((BEDA.))* Others simply: *Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice,* etc., *as far as* as also that word: *He that shall look on a woman to lust after, hath already committed adultery with her ((Matth. V))*. ((HIER.)) The cock crows: Peter denies thrice, etc., *as far as* and he washed away the filth of the threefold denial with tears.

*Gethsemani. ((ID.))* That is, the valley of fat ones, where fat bulls beset him and many calves surrounded him. *Sit ye here. ((ISID.))* They are separated in prayer who are separated in the passion: because he prays, while they sleep, weighed down by the fatness of the heart. *Till I pray. ((BED.))* When the Lord prays on the mountain, etc., *as far as* whence: *He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death. And greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends ((Phil. II; Joan. XV))*.

*And he began to fear. ((HIER.))* We are taught to fear and to be sorrowful before the judgment of death, we who cannot say of ourselves, save through him: *The prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not anything ((Joan. XIV))*.
*My soul is sorrowful,* etc. ((BED.)) He is not sorrowful because of death, etc., *as far as* but from the sleep of unbelief and from the torpor of the mind.

*And he prayed. ((ID.))* This voice is the sound of our infirmity, etc., *as far as* but because it will not be otherwise, *Not what I will, but what thou wilt.*

((HIER.)) This is against the Eutychians, who say that there is in Christ only one operation, one will: but here he shows the human, which through the infirmity of the flesh refuses the passion, and the divine, which is ready to accomplish the dispensation.
*But not what I will. ((HIER.))* Even to the end he ceases not to teach us to obey our fathers: and to set their will before our own.

*And he says to Peter,* etc. He who had said: *And if it behove me to die with thee, I will not deny thee: even if all shall be scandalized, yet not I ((Matth. XXVI))*; now, through the greatness of his sorrow, cannot overcome sleep.

*That ye enter not.* He does not say, that ye be not tempted, but *that ye enter not into temptation,* that is, that temptation may not overcome you, may not hold you within its nets.

((HIER.)) He enters into temptation who neglects to pray. Thrice the disciples sleep, thrice the Lord in prayer rouses them. The threefold sleeping signifies the three dead whom the Lord raised up. The first in the house, the second at the sepulchre, the third out of the sepulchre. The Lord's threefold watching teaches us that we have three persons in praying, and to ask pardon both for things past and for things present and for things to come. *But the flesh is weak. ((BEDA.))* For the flesh by its own weight ever draws to the lowest things.

*Arise.* After he had prayed the third time, he taught that the fear of the apostles was to be corrected by penance, and goes untroubled to the passion, saying: *Arise, let us go.* As if he should say, let them not find us fearing, but let us go of our own accord to meet them, so that, we being about to suffer, they may see joy and confidence.
*A sign. ((HIER.))* He gives the sign of a kiss with the venom of the devil: as Cain offered a sacrifice guileful and reprobate, whence they set wine with vinegar upon the cross.
*Rabbi. ((BEDA.))* With shameless and wicked assurance he calls him master, etc., *as far as* he fulfils that also: *With them that hated peace ((Psal. CXIX))*, etc.

*One. ((ID.))* Peter, according to John, with the same ardour of mind as in the rest. For he knew that Phinees, by punishing the sacrilegious, had received the reward of justice and of a perpetual priesthood. Luke says: *That the Lord touched the ear and healed it ((Luc. XXII))*. For he himself never forgets loving-kindness, and suffers not even his own enemies to be wounded. Mystically: teaching that they who in consenting to his death contracted a wound of the soul can, if they have worthily repented, deserve salvation.

*As to a robber. ((ID.))* As if he should say: It is foolish to seize with swords and clubs one who delivers himself up to you of his own accord: and by night, as though he were in hiding, to hunt him out by means of a traitor, when daily he teaches in the temple. But therefore you gather against me in darkness, because your power is in darkness.
*Then,* etc. ((ID.)) That is fulfilled which he said, that all should be scandalized, etc., *as far as* and they that were to be called back by God learned to give to their adversaries.

*But he,* etc. As Joseph, leaving his cloak behind, fled naked out of the hands of the unchaste mistress. But whoever wishes to escape the hands of the wicked, let him leave in mind the things that are of the world, and flee after Jesus. *From them.* Whose presence he loathed, and whose deeds. Not from the Lord, whose love, though absent in body, he kept fixed in his mind.

*The high priest,* etc. Caiphas, namely, who according to John was the high priest of that year, concerning whom Josephus writes to the same effect, that he had bought the high priesthood for himself from the Roman prince without any merit of worth: what wonder then, if an unjust high priest judges unjustly?

*Afar off. ((BEDA.))* Because he was near to denial, had he been near to Christ he would not have denied: in this, nevertheless, he is to be admired, that he did not leave the Lord even though he fears. That he fears is of nature, that he follows is of devotion: that he denies is of stealth, that he repents is of faith. *The court. ((HIER.))* The court is the worldly circuit. The servants are the demons. The fire is fleshly desire, and he who abides with these is not able to weep for his sins. *And he warmed himself. ((BEDA.))* There is a fire of charity; whereof it is said, etc., *as far as* and forthwith he set the secret places of his heart aflame with the coals of love.

*False testimony. ((ID.))* He is false who does not understand things said in the same sense in which they are said, etc., *as far as* so that he may seem to have spoken properly of the Jewish temple.

*And rising up,* etc. Being angry, because he found no place for calumny, he shows by the motion of his body the madness of his mind. *Not answering,* etc. He provokes him to an answer, that from any occasion of speech he may find place for accusing. But Jesus answered not, because he foresaw that whatever he should answer would be turned into calumny.

*Thou art Christ. ((HIER.))* Whom he was awaiting from afar, him he did not see near at hand: as Isaac, with darkened eyes, did not know Jacob under his hands, but long afterwards sings of things to come concerning him.

*And you shall see.* The priest asks after the Son of God; Jesus answers the Son of man; that we may understand the same to be Son of God and Son of man, lest we make a quaternity in the Trinity, and that man may be in God and God in man. *On the right hand of power.* Because *he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross: for which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above every name* ((Phil. II)).

*With the clouds of heaven. ((HIER.))* He ascended in a cloud, with a cloud he will come: that is, he ascended with his own body alone, which he took from the Virgin, and he is to come to judgment with the manifold Church, which is his body and his fulness, as Matthew says: But when the Son of man shall come, and all the angels with him, etc.

*But the high priest. ((BEDA.))* The same madness which before had shaken him from his seat, etc., *as far as* they did, when in Lycaonia they were honoured as gods. *His garments,* etc. ((HIER.)) That is, they lost the ephod in which the Jews had their honour, etc., *as far as* yet her chastity remains inviolate even to the consummation of the world in those whom the lot of election shall find.

*Who all,* etc. ((HIER.)) That by his own guilt he might loose our guilt, etc., *as far as* hence the prophet: *What shall I render to the Lord for all the things that he hath rendered to me? ((Psal. CXV.))*

*To cover the face,* etc. Not that he might not see their crimes, but that, as they themselves once did to Moses, they might hide from themselves the grace of the knowledge of him. This veil remains upon their heart until this day, which is taken away for them that believe in Christ. Whence, at his dying, it was as though the temple was rent, and the secret things of the holy of holies laid open.

*They struck him with the palms of their hands. ((BEDA.))* He who was then struck with blows is now struck with the blasphemies of false Christians. He who was consumed with the spittle of unbelievers is now dishonoured by the raving reproaches of the faithful.

*But he,* etc. Note that he denies Christ who denies that he is his disciple. For the Lord did not say: Thou shalt deny thyself to be my disciple, but *thou shalt deny me.* He denied him therefore when he denied that he was his disciple.

*And he went forth without,* etc. ((HIER.)) Peter, without the Spirit, yielded to the voice of a maidservant, etc., *as far as* and we go forth outside of what we were.

*For thou art also a Galilean. ((BEDA.))* The Galileans and the men of Jerusalem have the same tongue, but nevertheless every province and region has its own sound of speaking, which to change, etc., *as far as* because the men of Jerusalem sounded that name in one way, and the Galileans in another.

*And he remembered. ((ID.))* Peter denies by night, at the cock's crowing he repents. By day he professed three times that he loved him whom he had three times denied. For that which, etc., *as far as* he goes forth without (as the other Evangelists relate), that, set apart from the ungodly, he may the more freely wash away the guilt of his denial with tears.

*And straightway,* etc. There follows: *Binding Jesus.* It was the custom of the Jews that whomsoever they had adjudged to death they should deliver bound to the judge. And it is to be noted that they had not bound him then for the first time, but as soon as he was seized by night in the garden, as John says: And thus *they led him away to Annas first ((Joan. XVIII))*.

((HIER.)) Here is Samson bound by Dalila. Samson is interpreted, etc., *as far as* and he opens to us who thirst the fountain of everlasting life, that is, of his own body.

*Art thou the king of the Jews?* When Pilate asks of no crime save whether he be the king of the Jews, the impiety of those men is convicted who found not even falsely anything to lay against him. *Thou sayest.* So he tempers his answer that he speaks the truth, and yet gives no occasion to calumny. And note that to Pilate, who bears the sentence unwillingly, he answered in some part: but to the priests and the chief men he would not answer, and judged them unworthy of his speech.
*See,* etc. The heathen condemns Jesus, but refers the cause to the people of the Jews. *See in how many things,* etc.

*That rather Barabbas. ((BEDA.))* Their own petition cleaves to the Jews unto this day, which with all their labour they obtained. For, the choice being given them, they chose a robber instead of Jesus, a murderer instead of the Saviour. Deservedly therefore they lost salvation and life, and gave themselves over to robberies and seditions so far that they lost their kingdom and their country, and never received again the liberty of body and of soul.

*But Pilate.* Pilate gave many occasions of freeing the Saviour, first in comparing the robber with the just one, then in bringing forward: *What will you then that I do to the king of the Jews?* And when they had answered: *Let him be crucified,* he did not at once give in, but according to the suggestion of his wife, who had sent to him (as Matthew says): *Have thou nothing to do with that just man ((Matth. XXVII))*, answering he said: *Why, what evil hath he done?* And in saying this he acquitted Jesus. *But they the more,* etc. David: *Many dogs have encompassed me ((Psal. XXI))*, etc. Isaias: *I looked that he should do judgment, and behold iniquity: and justice, and behold a cry ((Isa. V))*. Jeremias: *My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me ((Jer. XII))*.

*Barabbas, and delivered,* etc. ((HIER.)) These are the two goats, the one apompeius, that is, the emissary, is loosed and sent away with the sin of the people into the desert of hell. The other is slain as a lamb for the sins of those who are loosed. The Lord's portion is always sacrificed, the devil's portion, who is their master, is hurled unbridled into Tartarus.

*Jesus with scourges.* That he might free us from scourges; whence: *The scourge shall not come nigh thy dwelling ((Psal. XC))*: whereas before it was said: *Many are the scourges of the sinner ((Psal. XXXI))*.

*((BEDA.)) Jesus scourged with whips.* He was scourged by Pilate himself, whence John: *Pilate took Jesus and scourged him:* and afterwards he added: *And the soldiers platting a crown of thorns ((Joan. XIX))*, etc. And he gave him over to the soldiers to be mocked. This he did for this end, that being sated with his punishments and reproaches they might not thirst further after his death.

*And they clothe him. ((BEDA.))* Matthew thus: *And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak about him ((Marc. XXVII))*. Which is the same thing. For it was given in place of the royal purple, etc., *as far as* she is clothed in purple or in scarlet, when in the triumph of the glorious martyrs she glories.

*And they struck,* etc. The head of Christ is God. They therefore strike the head of Christ who deny him to be God. And they who defend their error by the authority of Scripture (because writing is wont to be made with a reed) strike his head as it were with a reed. They spit in his face who spurn the presence of his grace with execrable words conceived out of the inward madness of a blind mind, and deny that he came in the flesh.

*They adored him.* As though he had falsely called himself God. But today (which is of a graver madness) certain men adore him with sure faith as true God, yet by their perverse deeds forthwith despise his words as though they were fables, and set the promises of his kingdom after the enticements of things temporal.

*And they lead him out. ((HIER.))* Here Abel is led out into the field by his brother to be slain. Here is Isaac, etc., *as far as* here is Jonas, cast out from the wood of the ship and into the sea and into the belly of the whale for three days.

*That they might crucify him. ((HIER.))* What is the very shape of the cross but the form of the four-square world? The east shines from the power, the right hand holds the north, the south stands at the left, the west is made firm beneath the feet. Whence the Apostle: *That we may know what is the breadth, the length, the height and the depth ((Ephes. III))*. Birds fly to the upper air in the form of a cross, a man adores, and swims, in the form of a cross, a ship is driven through the seas by a yard-arm made like to a cross. The letter Tau shows the sign of salvation and of the cross .

*And they forced. ((BEDA.))* The Lord himself first bore his own cross, as John says: afterwards this Simon, of whom the others also speak, and this in an order of mystery altogether fitting. *For Christ suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps ((Joan. XIX; I Petr. II))*.

((HIER.)) Simon, who bears the cross under compulsion, is he who labours for human praise. Men force him to this labour whom the fear or the love of God does not force.

*The father of Alexander.* This Simon seems to have been of great repute, since his sons also are marked out by name as being known to all.

((HIER.)) Some are called to mind through the merits of their fathers, others through the merits of their sons. But this Simon, etc., *as far as* whence: by Jeremias it is said to Judea: *A plentiful olive tree, fair, fruitful, goodly, the Lord called thy name.*

*The place of Calvary. ((HIER.))* The Jews hand down that in this place of the mountain the ram was offered for Isaac ((Gen. XXII)), that there Christ might be made bald, that is, might be severed from his own flesh, namely from carnal Judea.

((BEDA.)) Outside the gate the heads of the condemned were struck off, and the places of the beheaded are called calvaries. Therefore the Lord was crucified there, that where was the threshing-floor of the condemned, there the standards of the martyrs might be raised up. And because for us was made the curse of the cross, and he was both scourged and crucified for the salvation of all, he willed to be crucified as one guilty among the guilty.

*And they gave. ((BEDA.))* Matthew, *mingled with gall ((Matth. XXVII))*, which is the same thing. For he put gall for bitterness. For wine mingled with myrrh is most bitter; although it may be that they made the wine most bitter with both gall and myrrh.

*((HIER.)) And they gave,* etc. By this vinegar the juice of the deadly apple is wiped away. *And he took it not.* That for which he suffers. Whence of him: *That which I took not away, I then paid ((Psal. LXVIII))*.

*And he took it not.* Matthew: *And when he had tasted, he would not drink.* Matthew shows that for us he tasted the bitterness of death, but on the third day rose again.

*And crucifying him. ((HIER.))* Here salvation is fastened upon a tree. First death was fastened upon a tree. The first tree was of the knowledge of good and evil; the second is for us a tree of good only, and of life. The stretching out of the first hand to the tree laid hold on death; the stretching out of the second found the life that had perished. By this wood are we carried over the billowy sea to the land of the living.

*His garments. ((BEDA.))* The garment of Christ, divided into four according to the number of the soldiers, signifies the Church distributed equally, that is, harmoniously, through the four quarters of the world.

((HIER.)) The garments of the Lord are the commandments with which his body is covered, which is the Church, because they are divided among the soldiers of the Gentiles, so that there are four orders while the faith is one, that is, the married, the widowed, the prelates, the set apart. They cast lots for the undivided tunic, which is peace and truth in all things, after the manner of a royal mantle or of a ring. *Casting lots. ((ID.))* Upon the tunic, namely, which was without seam. Here the things allotted, etc., *as far as* and the lot comes or falls by the judgment of God alone.

*Now it was the third hour. ((HIER.))* This Mark has properly, for at the sixth hour darkness overspread the earth, so that none could move his head. For from the thirtieth, etc., *as far as* who are rather to be said to have crucified him, though they strive to dissemble it, than the soldiers, who according to their office obeyed their captain.

*And there was a title. ((BEDA.))* The title shows that not even by killing him could they bring it about that he should not be their king; whence: *But I am appointed king by him,* etc. For he is fittingly at once king and priest, since he offered to the Father the excellent victim of his own flesh upon the altar of the cross, and held forth the dignity of a king by the title, that he might make known to all that through the gibbet of the cross he had not lost, but had confirmed, his empire.

*And with him they crucify. ((BEDA.))* As the Apostle says: *Our old man is crucified together with him, that the body of sin may be destroyed, that sin may no more have dominion over us.* So long therefore as our works act, that the body of sin may be emptied out, so long, etc., *as far as* whence the Apostle: *That, being rooted and founded in charity, you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth, the length, the height and the depth ((Ephes. III))*. *Two thieves.* ((ID.)) The thieves who were crucified with the Lord signify those who, by faith and confession of Christ, or by the struggle of their own martyrdom, undergo any strict continence whatsoever. And they who do this for eternal glory are signified by the merit and the faith of the thief on the right. But whoever does it for human glory or with any less worthy intention imitates the mind and the deeds of the thief on the left.

((HIER.)) Truth, reckoned among the wicked, leaves the one on the left and takes up the other on the right; so will he do in the day of judgment, out of a like crime they obtain unlike ways. The one goes before Peter into paradise, the other before Judas into hell. A short confession purchases a long life, and a blasphemy that has an end is punished with an eternal penalty. Here the colt of Juda is bound to the vine, ἀναβόλαιον, that is, the cloak is dyed in the blood of the grape, here the kids tear the vineyard.
*Wagging their heads. ((HIER.))* The death of the wicked is sent forth when the bonds of hell are stirred up even to the neck, which is the neck of the human race.

*He saved others. ((HIER.))* Even unwilling they confess that he made others safe, and they condemn themselves by their own sentence, because he made others safe and could have saved himself if he would.

*Let him now come down.* It is more to rise from the sepulchre, and yet they did not believe. *These all have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together ((Psal. XIII))*.

*And they that were with him. ((BEDA.))* According to Luke ((Luc. XXIII)) one thief blasphemed, saying: *If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.* The other, etc., *as far as* they who seek heavenly things without doubt attain to them, Christ mediating and having mercy.

*And when the sixth hour was come. ((BEDA.))* It is to be noted that at the sixth hour, that is, when the sun was about to withdraw from the centre of the world, he was crucified, and that at daybreak, at the rising of the sun, he rose again, etc., *as far as* and at what hour the first Adam by sinning brought death into the world, at that same hour the second Adam by dying should destroy death.

*Darkness. ((HIER.))* Here is Noe made drunk and stripped, covered by heaven and earth with a drunkard's cloak, and mocked by man, here blood dripped from the wood.

*And some,* etc. Not all. Perhaps the Roman soldiers, not understanding the property of the Hebrew tongue, from that which is said Eloi, thought that Elias was being called upon by him. Or the Jews, perverting the Lord's words in their accustomed speech, defamed him of weakness, in that he was calling for the help of Elias.

*And running,* etc. ((BEDA.)) John says more fully: *Afterwards Jesus, knowing,* etc. As if: This you have done the less, give what you are. For they were, etc., *as far as* whereof: *The Lord planted the vine Soreth: and how art thou turned into the bitterness of a strange vine: and I looked that thou shouldst bring forth grapes, and thou hast brought forth thorns ((Isa. V))*.

*But Jesus,* etc. ((BEDA.)) Luke discloses what he said: *Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit; and saying this he expired ((Luc. XXIII))*. But that which John says: *When he had taken the vinegar, he said: It is consummated: and bowing his head he delivered up the spirit ((Joan. XIX))*. Between this which he says: *It is consummated,* and that: *bowing his head he sent forth the spirit,* there was sent forth that great voice which John passes over in silence, and the rest record: *Into thy hands,* etc.

((HIER.)) For, the flesh being made weak, the divine power straightway prevailed, which says: *Open ye to me the gates of justice ((Psal. CXVII))*, etc. But we who are of the earth die with no voice, or with one; for he expired with a lifted-up voice who came down from heaven.

*And the veil of the temple.* That the ark of the testament and all the mysteries of the law which were covered may appear, and may pass over to the Gentiles. Before it was said: *God is known in Judea, in Israel his name is great ((Psal. LXXV))*; but now: *Be thou exalted above the heavens, O God ((Ibid. LVI))*, *and in all,* etc.; and in the Gospel before: *Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles ((Matth. X))*.; and after the passion: *Go ye, and teach all nations ((Ibid. XXVIII))*.

*And seeing,* etc. It is shown why the centurion wonders, because he saw that he had so expired, that is, had sent forth his spirit. For no one has the power of sending forth his spirit, save the creator of souls.

*Truly,* etc. ((HIER.)) Note that the centurion before the cross, in the very scandal of the passion, confesses him truly the Son of God: and Arius, etc., *as far as* and, the Synagogue keeping silence, he affirms him truly the Son of God.

*And there were. ((ID.))* As the female sex is not shut out from salvation through Mary the Virgin: so it is not driven back from the mystery of the cross, of knowledge and of the resurrection, through the widow Mary Magdalen and the other mothers.

*Of James the less and of Joseph. ((BEDA.))* By James the less he means James the son of Alpheus, who is also the brother of the Lord, in that he was the son of Mary the Lord's mother's sister. Of whom John: *Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother ((Joan. XIX))*, etc. He seems to call her Cleophas's from her father or from her kindred.

*And when it was now evening,* etc. ((ID.)) Παρασκευὴ in Greek, preparation in Latin. By this name the Jews dwelling among the Greeks called the sixth day of the week, because on it they prepared the things that were needful for the sabbath, according as, etc., *as far as* until, the eighth age coming, the bodies themselves also, by the resurrection glorified, may together with the souls receive the incorruption of the eternal inheritance.

*Joseph came. ((HIER.))* Joseph came in the evening of the parasceve from Arimathia, which is interpreted *laying down,* to lay down the body of Christ, etc., *as far as* the elect, who are the stars of the sea, looking on from afar, when, if it can be done, even the elect shall be scandalized.

*And Joseph,* etc. ((BEDA.)) From the simple burial of the Lord the ambition of the rich is condemned, who not even in their tombs, etc., *as far as* celebrates with earthly linen, as the body of the Lord was buried in a clean linen cloth: so was it decreed by pope Sylvester.

*Which was hewn out. ((BEDA.))* It is said that the Lord's monument was a round house hewn out of the underlying rock, of such a height that a man standing upright can scarcely reach the top with his hand stretched out. And it has an entrance, etc., *as far as* but the colour of the monument and of the tomb is said to be mingled of white and red.

*And Mary,* etc. ((ID.)) Luke says: *That all his acquaintance stood afar off, and the women that had followed him ((Luc. XXIII))*. But when the others, his body being laid down, had returned to their own, the women alone, etc., *as far as* and they weigh carefully, with pious curiosity, whether haply they may be able to imitate him, and in what order his passion is to be embraced.
